q: Pre-norm vs post-norm?
short: Post-norm normalises after adding the residual (Norm(h + F(h))); pre-norm normalises the sub-layer input (h + F(Norm(h))), leaving an un-normalised residual path that carries gradients directly, so deep models train more stably.
detail: Final norm before output in pre-norm.
mistakes: Saying pre-norm removes the need for normalisation.

q: What is RMSNorm?
short: A normalisation that divides each vector by its root-mean-square and applies a learned gain, without subtracting the mean or adding a bias: cheaper than LayerNorm with similar quality.
follow: How much compute does it save?

q: How does RoPE encode position?
short: It rotates each pair of query and key dimensions by an angle proportional to the token's position (different frequencies per pair), so their dot product depends on relative distance.
mistakes: Adding RoPE to the input embeddings.

q: What is GELU?
short: Gaussian Error Linear Unit z·Φ(z): a smooth ReLU-like activation that passes small negative values and has no kink at zero.

q: What is SwiGLU?
short: A gated feed-forward layer: W_down[SiLU(W_gate x) ⊙ W_up x]. The SiLU gate controls what content passes; with width ~8d/3 it matches a 4d MLP's parameters and performs better.

q: What is a Mixture of Experts layer?
short: Many expert feed-forward networks plus a router; each token is sent to the top-k experts and their outputs are combined with gate weights, so only a fraction of parameters is active per token.
follow: Where is MoE placed in the block?

q: An MoE layer has 8 experts of 134M parameters with top-2 routing. Stored vs active?
short: Stored 8 × 134M ≈ 1.07B; active per token 2 × 134M = 268M (25%).

q: What does MoE not save?
short: Memory: all experts must be stored (and loaded on accelerators) even though few run per token; there is also routing and communication overhead.
detail: Compute per token is what drops.
mistakes: Assuming MoE models fit small GPUs.

q: Why does post-norm struggle at depth?
short: Every gradient must pass through each layer's normalisation, which rescales it; across many layers this distorts gradient magnitudes near the input, requiring warm-up and causing instability. Pre-norm's identity path avoids that.

q: Show why RoPE gives relative position.
short: Rotation matrices satisfy R(mθ)ᵀR(nθ) = R((n − m)θ), so (R_m q)·(R_n k) = qᵀR((n − m)θ)k, a function of the distance only.
detail: Applied per dimension pair with different θ.

q: Verify SwiGLU's parameter matching at d = 4096.
short: Plain MLP: 2 · d · 4d = 8d² ≈ 134.2M. SwiGLU: 3 · d · (8d/3) = 8d² ≈ 134.2M.

q: Why is load balancing needed in MoE?
short: Routers drift toward a few experts, which then get more updates and more traffic while others stay untrained; overloaded experts exceed capacity and drop tokens. An auxiliary loss and capacity limits keep usage even.

q: Dense 70B vs MoE with 47B total / 13B active: compare.
short: The MoE needs memory for ~47B parameters but compute per token like a ~13B model, so it is faster per token than the dense 70B while needing less memory than it; quality can approach larger dense models but serving needs multi-GPU memory and routing support.
mistakes: Comparing active MoE size to dense total.

q: What is expert capacity?
short: The maximum tokens an expert processes per batch, set as capacity factor × fair share; tokens beyond it are dropped from that layer (passed through the residual) or rerouted.
detail: Trade-off between drops and wasted padding.

q: LayerNorm vs RMSNorm vs BatchNorm for LLMs?
short: BatchNorm depends on batch statistics, awkward for variable-length sequences and inference; LayerNorm normalises per token; RMSNorm is LayerNorm without centring, cheaper and standard in recent LLMs.

q: How can RoPE help extend context length?
short: Rescale RoPE frequencies (position interpolation, NTK-aware or YaRN-style scaling) so positions beyond the training length map to rotation angles seen in training, then briefly fine-tune on longer sequences.

q: Design an MoE layer for a 7B-active model.
short: Pick experts and k (e.g. 8 experts, top-2, or many fine-grained experts plus a shared expert), set capacity factor ~1.25, add load-balancing (and router z) losses, use expert parallelism across GPUs with all-to-all communication, and monitor per-expert utilisation.
detail: Memory per GPU and communication dominate.

q: Why might gated FFNs outperform plain MLPs?
short: Multiplicative gating lets the layer compute input-dependent feature selection (second-order interactions) cheaply, giving more expressiveness per parameter and smoother optimisation; the benefit is largely established empirically.

q: Do MoE experts specialise in topics?
short: Loosely and often syntactically rather than by human topics: routing correlates with token types (code, punctuation, numbers, some languages); specialisation is learned and partly entangled, so experts aren't clean topic modules.

q: Which of these changes affect inference cost, and how?
short: RMSNorm: slight speed-up. RoPE: negligible, enables longer contexts. SwiGLU: same parameters, similar cost. MoE: lower compute per token but more memory and communication; batching across experts matters.
detail: KV cache variants (M5) matter more for decode.
follow: Which matters most at long context?
mistakes: Assuming architecture tweaks are free at serving.
